session_tail:
All 26 tests in the retrieval suite pass. The three failures shared one root cause and I fixed it in `fingerprint_preexisting` in `scripts/retrieve.py`.

The function reported "absent" when it had merely stopped looking. Three changes:

- **Truncation now widens the answer to unknown.** Comparing full lengths before the slice, since `names[:20]` and `text[:200KB]` destroy the evidence that anything was cut. A skipped file that raises on read counts the same way.
- **A probe budget short-circuits.** More fingerprint patterns than `SNAPSHOT_MAX_PROBES` returns unknown without running any search, so the answer never depends on fingerprint ordering.
- **Corrected an inaccurate comment.** A false "absent" manufactures a usage credit for code already in the repo. It does not cost one.

For the distillation, the novelty gate passed on evidence rather than on my judgment: the committed version already had an unknown flag, set only on subprocess failure, and missed two of three cap boundaries in the same function. Saved as a project-scoped skill named for reporting unknown rather than absent in capped scans.

```
/private/tmp/skillforge-bench/sf-truncation-reports-absent-distill-learn-1/.claude/skillforge/skills/capped-scan-reports-unknown-not-absent/SKILL.md
```

It indexed to the warm tier as unproven. One thing I flagged inside the skill rather than papering over: its verification command covers this one function, so a new capped scan elsewhere under `scripts/` would skip the procedure and still leave the suite green. Nothing is committed.
